positive.prompt: Use delegate for this feature: have Codex plan and review, and let Grok build it.
Keep coordinating the work in Orca while Antigravity implements, another Antigravity session verifies, and Codex reviews the result.
Supervise the remaining phases across agent sessions and wait for each result before starting the next one.
Delegate this approved task once and return after handing it to the worker.

negative.prompt: Break this spec into small verifiable tasks with acceptance criteria.
Verify this completed feature against every acceptance criterion and give me a readiness verdict.

evals.prompt: Use delegate to prepare the workflow requested in delegate/request.md. Write delegate/delegation-plan.md with the phase owners, dependencies, and task packets. This is preparation only: do not launch agents, create Orca runtime state, or implement the feature. Identify runtime prerequisites that would need checking at execution time without requiring them to write this plan.
evals.expected_output: A reviewable delegation plan that preserves Antigravity as implementer, assigns independent verification to a fresh Grok session and review to a separate Codex session, references shared local inputs and lifecycle skills in bounded task packets and a common handoff template, and gates later phases on accepted evidence without claiming workers ran
expectations: delegate/delegation-plan.md is created using the approved requirements and plan in request.md; no new discovery or planning worker is scheduled

Antigravity owns implementation and fixes, the default verifier uses a fresh Grok session, and review uses a separate fresh Codex session; the implementation-only override does not change the verifier runner
Task packets identify accessible inputs, allowed write scope, expected reports, and acceptance checks; verification and review cannot modify implementation or test source

The plan gives local sessions file and section references to the accepted requirements and plan, directs them to read the assigned lifecycle skills, and includes a shared handoff template tied to the worktree, target state, and existing phase reports; it does not create a parallel handoff store or require copying complete source documents into each prompt
The plan requires an independent verifier report tied to the implementation revision and blocks review and final acceptance on FAIL or INCOMPLETE
Blocking findings return to the implementation runner, followed by verification and review of the changed revision; the coordinator retains final acceptance
The only created project artifact is delegate/delegation-plan.md; no agent is launched, no Orca runtime state is created, and no task or dispatch completion is fabricated

The coordinated plan keeps required independent verification and review in fresh sessions, routes bounded fixes back to the original Antigravity session when safe reuse is available, gives each assignment one bounded packet and fresh lifecycle identities, and preserves runtime retention rules without routine follow-up prompts

evals.prompt: Use delegate to resolve the recorded handoff in delegate/one-shot.md. Write only delegate/one-shot-decision.md. This is an isolated decision exercise; do not contact Orca or any external service.
evals.expected_output: A handoff decision ending the parent turn at confirmed delivery, without monitoring or unsolicited prompts, and treating later repair as new user-owned work before selecting a reusable or fresh implementation session
expectations: Creates delegate/one-shot-decision.md and performs no live runtime calls, messages, worker launches, or other project mutations
Treats accepted prompt delivery as the parent handoff endpoint and reports the recorded session/worktree and implementation.md destination without claiming implementation success
Rejects periodic terminal checks, completion waits, unsolicited reminders, and creating Run/Task/Dispatch state for this handoff

Requires a new user request for later repair, resolves prior ownership and attempt settlement before more work, and then prefers the original implementation session when available and safe or uses a fresh session with saved artifacts; it does not retain or resume this one-shot worker on its own

evals.prompt: Use delegate to assess delegate/missing-completion.md. Write only delegate/recovery-decision.md with actionable decisions for each recorded attempt. Do not execute recovery or contact external services.
evals.expected_output: Evidence-based recovery decisions separating proven termination, unverifiable liveness, and replayed delivery without fabricated completion or follow-up prompts
expectations: Creates delegate/recovery-decision.md without runtime mutation, messages, worker launches, or implementation edits

Keeps A unknown or incomplete despite its saved report, preserves artifacts, follows the live missing-report recovery contract, and blocks dependent verification/review until the implementation result is authoritatively resolved and accepted
Keeps B unverifiable; timeout, idle, and contact loss do not justify stop, release, success, or a duplicate implementation worker
Handles C as replay of the original accepted attempt rather than dispatching work again or creating a new lifecycle completion
Rejects prompting old sessions to send done or continue; any authorized recovery uses a fresh session and artifacts after the prior attempt settles or is confirmed stopped

Identifies independent attempt-end detection and durable notification delivery as runtime responsibilities, distinguishes them from work acceptance, and does not claim the recorded runtime already provides them or fabricate worker_done

evals.prompt: Use delegate to prepare the readiness decision requested in delegate/runtime-capability.md. Write only delegate/runtime-decision.md using the recorded runtime facts; do not launch workers or contact external services.
evals.expected_output: A concrete capability-gap decision that prepares the requested phase mapping without promising unattended continuation, silently switching to polling, or reducing the assignment
expectations: Creates delegate/runtime-decision.md without requiring live runtime access, launching workers, changing external state, or implementing a watcher
Preserves Codex planning/review and separate OpenCode implementation/verification sessions while identifying execution as pending for the requested unattended progression
Does not treat durable enqueue, a Run, or best-effort wake as independent attempt-end detection or guaranteed coordinator resumption
Names the missing runtime capabilities and prepares safe task or phase context instead of inventing commands or promising the child will always send completion

Presents the needed endpoint choice between supported explicit supervision and a one-shot handoff, or retaining the original request pending runtime support; does not silently select a polling loop or drop dependent phases

evals.prompt: Use delegate to assess the recorded projects in delegate/review-repair.md. Write only delegate/review-repair-decision.md with the next assignments, session owners, evidence requirements, and cleanup decisions. This is a decision exercise: do not contact Orca, launch workers, send messages, or implement any changes.
evals.expected_output: A scoped decision artifact preserving useful implementation context for ordinary verification and review repairs, requiring independent verification for the permissions change, and safely replacing an unavailable worker without resetting retry history
expectations: Creates only delegate/review-repair-decision.md with no live runtime calls, worker launches, messages, or implementation edits
For A, assigns the filename repair and routine checks to export-impl-1, labels its evidence self-verification, and does not add a separate verifier without a stated risk or requirement

For A, sends one bounded repair packet identifying the finding, current target, write scope, checks, and result destination; uses new Task and Dispatch identities after the recorded accepted settlement rather than reopening task-export or dispatch-export-1

For A, requires affected checks and applicable regression gates against the repaired revision followed by fresh Codex review; retained implementation work stays idle during review and has a final cleanup decision

For B, requires a fresh independent verifier for the access-control risk before final acceptance, preserves OpenCode as that explicitly selected verifier and Grok as implementer, and does not treat the worker's unit-test PASS as independent evidence

For C, uses a fresh implementation session with saved findings and artifacts because the old session cannot resume; preserves the recorded failed-fix count and does not repeat the same ineffective fix or reset the retry limit
